emerging_technology: Agentic AI built on large language models (LLM-based agents that plan, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks)
intended_application: Proposed bounded applicant-support workflow: retrieve approved program information, ask clarifying questions, plan next steps, and request a counselor appointment through a permission-limited tool. Staff approve outbound messages and any record changes. Excludes admission, scholarship, visa and eligibility decisions.
industry_sector: Higher education - graduate and professional/continuing education recruitment. Peer group: professional and continuing education schools of research universities. Applicant trust, privacy, accessibility and accuracy matter; exact legal obligations require specialist review.
business_need: Scenario hypothesis: reduce repetitive inquiry handling and improve timely guidance. Actual demand, response time and benefits have not been measured.
users_stakeholders: Prospective students, admissions counselors, marketing/enrollment staff, university IT and compliance officers
adoption_posture: Moderate / fast-follower is a course-case assumption, not an official NYU policy.
capabilities_constraints: Scenario assumptions: existing staff and approved content; potential CRM integration not verified. SPS's public admissions page already offers a chatbot named Violet (D18); its design is not disclosed.
risk_consequence_context: Wrong deadlines or promises can harm applicants; unauthorized actions can expose data. No applicant records are used. No legal determination is made.
management_question: How far have agentic AI and agent-based applicant support diffused, what is accelerating or inhibiting that diffusion, and what timing implication follows for SPS (without making the adoption decision)?
time_horizon: 12 months: decision on next evaluation step now, review within one admissions cycle
additional_context: Continuity with Assignments 2-4 (same technology, application and organization). A3: proposed incremental, sustaining process innovation; compare staff-only, simple retrieval and the proposed agent first. A4: agentic AI is a Breakthrough with an unresolved Potential-Promethean candidacy; Low weight on SPS's present decision (C3). Use the dated source register. EVIDENCE-QUALITY PROBE. A planning memo forwarded to the specialist asserts: (1) '82% of colleges use AI in admissions, so this is already mainstream' (D20); (2) '23% of organizations are scaling agentic AI, which is past the 16% chasm' (D5); (3) 'the UAE already has 64% adoption, so the U.S. will follow quickly' (D3); (4) '31% of developers use AI agents, so admissions offices will soon' (D8); (5) 'a university expects to save $800 per inquiry with recruitment agents' (D14). The memo asks the specialist to conclude that agent-based applicant support has crossed the chasm and that SPS is already late. These are planning assertions, not verified conclusions.
